applied.old: If you're sensitive, start lower and do the trial with just 50mg 5-HTP at night for 2–3 nights, then go up to 100mg if 50mg was clearly helpful and not causing side effects. You can also add 10–20mg P5P in the morning, like Scott did, especially if the 5-HTP felt like it "almost worked," as that could be a sign it wasn't converting cleanly over to serotonin. Don't do the trial at the same time as the other suggested regimen changes (like UMP, agmatine, D-serine, psychedelics, or prescription medication changes), since the point is to see whether the 5-HTP itself is doing anything. If it's the right tool, the first things you'll usually notice are your mood or sleep quality improves, you have less nighttime rumination, and your dreams become more vivid or memorable.

applied.inserted: Tabernanthe elliptica ("bisexual" or "healer" iboga): an iboga cousin with many iboga alkaloids. In my experience it's the best of both worlds, but lower potency than regular iboga, and it doesn't feel as trancey. Try elliptica first for microdosing: in my experience it's more functional, more clear-headed, and often better for mood.

Agmatine with psychedelics is more complicated, and I can't say to take it with them or not. People's reports differ: some say it makes a trip or roll stronger while capping the euphoria, others that it weakens it. A friend of mine finds it gives a lot of the introspective benefits he gets from iboga, and that the two go well together, although I haven't heard of that from others. I don't notice much from it myself, aside from, I think, a lower ceiling on euphoria. I wouldn't use it unless a trip gets too stormy, but you can try the combination to see if it's worthwhile for you. Everyone's different.
